rows.topic: Sag & Tension Calculation with Wind and Ice
rows.textLatex: A transmission line conductor consists of hard drawn copper conductor $120\text{ mm}^2$ cross-section; the conductor used is $37/2.11\text{ mm}$ having weight of $1118\text{ kg/km}$ and has a span of $200\text{ meters}$. The supporting structures being level. The conductor has an ultimate tensile stress of $42.2\text{ kg/mm}^2$ and allowable tension is not to exceed $1/4^{\text{th}}$ of ultimate strength. Find (i) the sag in still air (ii) the sag with a wind pressure of $60\text{ kg/m}^2$ and an ice coating of $10\text{ mm}$. (iii) also find the vertical sag under the condition in (ii). Assume density of ice as $0.915\text{ gm/cc}$.
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of suspension insulators.
Discuss the advantages of V-string insulators.
Define charging current in underground cables. Also explain its effects on underground cables.

In a test for a fault to earth on a $520\text{ m}$ length of cable having a resistance of $1.1\text{ }\Omega$ per $1000\text{ m}$, the faulty cable is looped with a sound cable of the same length but having a resistance of $2.29\text{ }\Omega$ per $1000\text{ m}$. The resistances of the other two arms of the testing network at the balance are in the ratio of $2.7:1$. Calculate the distance to fault from the testing end of the cable.
With the help of a suitable diagram show that the insulation resistance of an underground cable varies inversely as its length.
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of overhead transmission line and underground cable.
Discuss the features of (i) cadmium copper conductor (ii) All Aluminum Conductor.
Calculate the minimum clearance of the lowest conductor above ground for a $132\text{ kV}$ and $400\text{ kV}$ transmission line.
Explain how the power factor of a consumer can be improved economically.
Explain availability factor.

rows.topic: Long Transmission Line Distributed Parameters & ABCD
rows.textLatex: A three phase $50\text{ Hz}$ transmission line delivers $18\text{ MW}$ at $110\text{ kV}$ at $0.9$ lagging power factor. The line is $180\text{ km}$ long and the conductors are placed at the corners of an equilateral triangle of $3\text{ m}$ side. The radius and resistance of each conductor are $0.6\text{ cm}$ and $0.2\text{ ohm per km}$. Determine i) A and B constants of the line ii) sending end voltage and iii) voltage regulation of the line. Assume that the line parameters are distributed throughout the length of the line.
